title: Over a field, at a smooth point the dimension equals the rank of the differentials
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] such that $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. Then $\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a finite-dimensional $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-vector space and $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ equals the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}S$ at the point $\mathfrak q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), implication (1) => (3); used in Smoothing 07CP (lines 1571-1576: 'the fibre ring of R -> D_k is smooth at q_k of dimension n')

proof.text:
(A standard smooth neighbourhood of the point.) By smoothness at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], choose $u\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $k	o S_u$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. The extended ideal $\mathfrak qS_u$ is prime. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-locally-standard-smooth] to $k	o S_u$ and $\mathfrak qS_u$: there is $v\in S_u\setminus\mathfrak qS_u$ such that $(S_u)_v$ has a standard smooth presentation [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], say with $n\ge c\ge0$. Write $v=a/u^m$ with $a\in S$. Since $v
otin\mathfrak qS_u$, we have $a
otin\mathfrak q$; hence $f=ua
otin\mathfrak q$. Localizing successively at $u$ and $v$ is isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to the principal localization $S_f$ (both invert $u$ and $a$, and $f=ua$; the mutually inverse maps follow from the universal property of localization), so transport gives a standard smooth presentation of $S_f$ with the same $n,c$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field), first paragraph: smoothness at q and Lemma 00TA (lemma-smooth-syntomic) give g not in q with S_g standard smooth over k

proof.text: (Differentials on the standard smooth neighbourhood.) Let $b_i\in S_f$ be the images of the variables in the standard smooth presentation from step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-kahler-basis], $\Omega_{S_f/k}$ is free over $S_f$ with basis $\mathrm db_{c+1},\dots,\mathrm db_n$, hence has rank $n-c$. The prime $\mathfrak q_f=\mathfrak qS_f$ has residue field canonically $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Tensoring the displayed basis with that field therefore gives a basis of $\Omega_{S_f/k}\otimes_{S_f}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ of cardinality $n-c$; in particular this vector space is finite-dimensional of dimension $n-c$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth), part (2), as used in the first paragraph of the proof of Lemma 00TT

proof.text: (Return to the original module of differentials.) By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], $\Omega_{S_f/k}\cong(\Omega_{S/k})_f=\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_SS_f$, with the isomorphism induced by localization. Tensoring over $S_f$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and using associativity of tensor products yields $\Omega_{S_f/k}\otimes_{S_f}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Thus the vector space in the statement is finite-dimensional of dimension $n-c$ by step 2.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize), part (2), implicit in the localization used in the proof of Lemma 00TT

proof.text: (Dimension comparison.) The standard open $D(f)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S$ contains $\mathfrak q$ and is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}S_f$, carrying $\mathfrak q$ to $\mathfrak q_f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace], the Krull dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ at $\mathfrak q$ equals that of $\operatorname{Spec}S_f$ at $\mathfrak q_f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-over-field-dimension-at-points] the latter is $n-c$. Together with step 3, this proves $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}(\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q))=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$.
